title: You know you're wrong. You defend it anyway.
hook: You know you were wrong. You'll still find ten reasons you were right.
caption: You know you were wrong and you defend it anyway. Cognitive dissonance makes us reinterpret the evidence instead of the decision. A bad call doesn't make you a bad person.
cta: Follow QuanTik for the psychology behind your money

thumb.footer: Simulated / sourced data • Educational, not advice
headline: WRONG.
STILL
DEFENDING.

scenes.say: You know you were wrong. You'll still find ten reasons you were right.
Cognitive dissonance: the pain of your actions and beliefs not matching.
The loop: make a decision, see proof it was wrong, feel bad, reinterpret the proof.
Admitting it hurts once. Defending it hurts a little, many times.
So we pick the second, and the loss quietly gets bigger.
Separate yourself from the decision. A bad call doesn't make you a bad person.

takeaway: Separate yourself from the decision. A bad call doesn't make you a bad person.
